cause: shafinMultitool/Multitool2Module/Models/CoreMLWrappers/DETRDetector.swift was rewritten between the historical commit and HEAD: the old extractDetections() merged every pixel of a class into one bounding box per class, the current one runs connected-component labelling and emits one box per component. More components therefore reach the critique, which is the intended behaviour (two separate lamps are two objects) but means object_count, objectDensity and background_clutterScore are NOT parity-comparable with the historical artifact.
consequence: Part of the residual drift against the historical numbers is a detector-input difference rather than a critique-rule difference. Rule alignment must be judged against the fresh baseline lane, not against the historical artifact.
question: Are the signals the critique consumes the same as in the historical artifact the alignment targets?
